cells.tense: You are here, and a season of your life is closing, and you can feel it close and stay open at once.
cells.act: let this moment be a fresh entry, not a continuation
cells.ask: When something comes wearing more of the same, stop and take it fresh. See what is actually here before you name it.
cells.core:
Something in you can close a chapter without sealing the book. You can say that's done and mean it, and still be standing in the open where the next thing hasn't been chosen yet. You don't need the ending to be tidy, or the next thing to be known. Both are allowed.

The move is small. When a moment arrives wearing the face of more of the same, take it fresh. Not because the old thing wasn't real, but because you're standing here now and this is the one arriving. Take it before you name it. The point isn't to finish faster or start sooner. It's to be at the door when it opens, rather than already talking to whoever's behind it.
cells.sheetLine: You can finish without shutting anything down.
cells.verb: finishing and letting the finished thing open the next
cells.place: the wide-open moment before anything has been chosen from it

cells.tense: You will announce the ending before it has happened, and then have to live inside a room that isn't actually finished yet.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Before the next ending gets announced, check whether it has happened. If it hasn't, leave it open and meet what is actually here.
cells.core:
Where this runs ahead of itself, the ending gets announced before it has happened. The waiting is hard — the unresolved thing has weight you'd rather put down — so the arrival is claimed early, and you're left standing in a finished room that isn't finished. It leaves you solid, and a little ahead of your own life.

The small move is to check before you say it. Next thing you reach to close, stop — is this actually done, or are the words early? If it isn't, leave it that way and let what's really here meet you. The ending will hold better when you don't have to rush it. You give up the comfort of the announcement and get to be where you actually are.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that has closed, and you are still standing there, still asking it to open.
cells.act: open the door to the next thing on time, not early
cells.ask: Take one finished thing and hold it as finished. Nothing needs to come after it this week.
cells.core:
Something ended, and you didn't let it. You keep going back to the door — the pursuit, the search, the version of it that might still turn into what you wanted. You are not short on possibility; you are refusing to let the last possibility be what it was. So the next thing hasn't had room to arrive. Anything new has to compete with something that's already over.

Here's the small move, and it asks for no effort. Take one finished thing and hold it as finished. Nothing needs to come after — no next step, no replacement. Holding it there is the whole of it. That's how the room clears: not by finding what you're looking for, but by finishing the search on time.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at a door that already closed behind you.
cells.verb: finishing and letting the finished thing open the next
cells.place: the wide-open moment before anything has been chosen from it

cells.tense: A cycle has ended without your noticing, and the same is true of one still going — and you keep moving through both as though neither were true.
cells.act: let go of the thing you are gripping
cells.ask: Notice something you are still carrying that has already finished. Put it down for today, without saying a word about it.
cells.core:
You keep going — and somewhere back there something ended, or something is still going, and you don't know which. The gripping happens before you notice you're doing it. You are not holding the past on purpose. You're carrying things you think are still live, and some of them have already finished their business with you.

This isn't work for more effort. It's release, and release doesn't need to know what it's releasing. Notice something you're holding that's already over — you'll know it by how tired your hand is — and put it down. Just for today, no ceremony, no declaration. It doesn't have to be important. Let it go and notice the space where your hand was.
cells.sheetLine: You carry things that have already finished with you.
cells.verb: finishing and letting the finished thing open the next
cells.place: the wide-open moment before anything has been chosen from it

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that the person has actually completed something — the record shows completed cycles present but not whether the person can see them; I only describe the seeing, not the thing itself, and I don't name what they finished. The reader's likely objection: 'nothing in my life is actually finished.' The asks survive that — each is a small noticing or a small letting go, doable even if no cycle has closed; the one that serves me more than them is any line that praises the completeness for them rather than reporting where their sight of it stands.
